title: Senior's toolkit: testing and enforcing access control
summary: Two accounts and curl, Burp's Autorize, ASP.NET Core's fallback policy and resource-based authorization, and PhysicalFileProvider for files.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: testing and enforcing access control
steps.body: Access control bugs are found with two accounts and patience, and prevented with rules that apply by default. These are the tools for both.

toolkit.what: The two-account test: capture every request as user A, replay it with user B's session, compare. Any 200 that should be a 404 is an IDOR or BFLA.
flags: print only the status, for loops over many ids
toolkit.example: for id in $(seq 1000 1010); do printf '%s ' $id; curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -b bob.jar https://staging.shop.example/api/orders/$id; done

toolkit.what: Automates the two-account test while you click through the app as a privileged user: every request is replayed with a low-privilege cookie and with none, and colour-coded as bypassed, enforced or unclear.
flags: paste the other user's Cookie header
a string ("Not found") that means the check worked
toolkit.example: Burp → Extensions → BApp Store → Autorize → paste 'Cookie: sid=<bob>' → Autorize is on → browse the admin pages as sam

toolkit.what: Deny by default in ASP.NET Core: every endpoint with no authorization metadata requires a signed-in user. Public endpoints opt out with AllowAnonymous().
flags: one policy on a whole group

toolkit.what: Resource-based authorization: the rule ("owner or shared with") lives in one AuthorizationHandler<TRequirement, TResource> and every endpoint asks it about the object it loaded.
flags: on failure, so ids cannot be probed

toolkit.what: Serve files from one folder only: it refuses absolute paths and paths that climb out of the root (GetFileInfo returns a NotFoundFileInfo).
flags: false for missing and for refused paths

steps.prompt: Match each tool or API to the job it does.
pairs: replays your requests with a second user's cookie
requires sign-in on endpoints that say nothing
checks one user against one loaded object
keeps file access inside one folder

steps.prompt: Loop over order ids with Bob's session and print only each status code.
code: for id in $(seq 1000 1010); do curl -s -o /dev/null __1__ '%{http_code}\n' __2__ bob.jar https://staging.shop.example/api/orders/$id; done

steps.prompt: With a fallback policy that requires a signed-in user, the health check endpoint `/healthz` starts returning 401 to the load balancer. What is the right fix?
options: Add `.AllowAnonymous()` to the `/healthz` endpoint, so the exception is explicit and visible in review
Give the load balancer an admin account
Move the health check to a secret path
steps.explain: Deny by default with explicit, greppable exceptions: a reviewer can list every `AllowAnonymous` in the codebase in one search.
